correct_answer: The correction has supervisor approval but lacks formal PM approval in the system per Section 5.4; Torres' emoji is not a system-of-record approval; the most significant risk is that the correction generates fee on THORNFIELD ($589) without CO notification, which could be construed as an improper cost transfer benefiting the contractor.
rationale: Section 5.4 requires both supervisor approval AND PM approval for corrections older than 60 days. David Holt's approval satisfies the supervisor requirement (Section 5.5 permits current supervisor when original is unavailable). However, Torres' thumbs-up emoji in Teams is NOT a formal approval in Costpoint — the system shows his approval is still PENDING. The more significant risk is the fee implication: moving costs from a T&M contract (no fee on hours) to a CPFF contract generates 8.2% fee ($589) that the government would not have paid under the original charging. Without CO notification per FAR 52.216-7(d), this creates the appearance of a cost transfer that benefits the contractor — exactly the kind of pattern DCAA flags as a potential deficiency finding. Answer A incorrectly treats the emoji as sufficient formal approval and downplays the fee risk. Answer B incorrectly reads Section 5.5 — Park's transfer to classified programs where she lacks system access makes her functionally 'unavailable.' Answer D overstates the 60-day policy — it requires additional approval, not VP exception; the policy is being followed (just incompletely), and a single correction is not a 'systemic deficiency.'
